method: 1526 print and suppression chronology plus autograph prison-letter evidence, with institutional and scholarly cross-check; late martyrdom formulas remain a separate transmission layer

important_deltas.finding: The 1535 autograph prison letter becomes a central primary artifact: Tyndale asks for warm clothing, a lamp, a Hebrew Bible, grammar and dictionary.
The famous final-prayer formula is not promoted to an exact direct quotation without a contemporary locator.
Cologne/Worms printing, English suppression, imprisonment and execution are treated as separate evidentiary stages instead of one continuous martyrdom legend.
The scale of Tyndale's later linguistic influence is not reduced to a single unsupported percentage or slogan.

unsupported_popular_claims.claim: Tyndale's famous final prayer is preserved as a verbatim contemporary transcript.
A single exact percentage can summarize how much of later English Bibles is Tyndale without a defined textual comparison method.

claim_upgrade_conditions.claim: famous final prayer as direct quotation
claim_upgrade_conditions.upgrade_requires: contemporary or near-contemporary source with exact wording, provenance and locator

claim_upgrade_conditions.claim: numeric share of Tyndale wording in a later Bible
claim_upgrade_conditions.upgrade_requires: defined edition pair, collation method, unit of comparison and reproducible count
